scope: Individual editorial reading of all compiled glossary terms and their dossier assignments. External checks are identified by URL on the affected terms. The working-language review considers adult and family reading; it does not measure reader performance.

terms.finding: Corrected the definition to require specified acts and intent directed at a protected group. The new examples are illustrative; identification of an act alone cannot establish intent.
Retained the later oral-history and memoir examples, which are essential for Partition. Changed the visible name to two words while preserving the link ID.
Ming and Mughal works illustrate commissioning and support. A patron’s role leaves the number and identities of individual makers open.
The Han tomb material is associated with people who arranged burial as well as the deceased. The qualification about whose beliefs the objects reflect is important.
In the Han entry, land, buildings and associated labor are concrete references for the model. Its depiction does not supply an owner’s balance sheet.
The Han and Egyptian examples require attribution of beliefs to particular settings. The definition makes their historical representation open to study.
Broadened the examples to include spoken testimony alongside written records and objects. This fits living community accounts as well as excavated material.
Colima’s selected figures support descriptions and interpretations with different levels of certainty. The definition uses that distinction directly.
Caral and Colima use different kinds of date ranges. The short definition allows both revised dates and uncertain ordering.
Repetition and shared meaning offer a starting point for Colima; shape alone cannot identify a particular act or belief.
A line of rulers is intelligible in imperial China and Mughal history. The family frame leaves room for conflict and changing institutions.
Diverse subjects and unequal power fit the Roman example; the word “often” avoids requiring identical conquest or government in every case.
The Roman use is appropriately gendered and identifies a previous legal status. It gives no automatic entitlement to citizenship, wealth or office.
Traveling together explains overland transport at Palmyra. It does not prescribe one animal species or a complete route for an individual object.
Words on a surface are identifiable on the Palmyra stone and the Kushan coin. A claim in an inscription still has an author and audience.
Issuing and using coins connects the Kushan object with an authority and users without treating circulation as a border map.
The core ownership-history meaning fits the museum examples; it leaves the archaeological findspot as a separate question. Dimensions such as loans or custody may also matter in particular cases.
The definition accommodates coastal and river connections and the transfer of both people and goods. A port name alone cannot trace an individual vessel.
The simple upright-monument description fits Aksum. Carving and writing are possible features rather than required features.
Material remains together with their contexts encompass tools, architecture and deposits in Colima and Moche. This avoids equating archaeology with collecting objects.
Directing water to fields fits the agricultural examples. Household water storage or an urban drain requires separate functional evidence.
Goods and labor under political demand are both possible in the Moche inquiry. The generic definition does not establish who owed what in that setting.
The term explains how subjects in an image are interpreted in context. The Moche example requires separate evidence for which figure or action is shown.
Rank, office and authority describe what the Benin example can communicate. Possession or resemblance alone cannot identify a specific historical officer.
Everyday things and prestige objects both fit. The example of a drum uses making, use and social relations rather than metal alone.
The definition makes coercion and denial of freedom explicit. Its use in Banda and Atlantic contexts should not be extended to every form of dependent labor.
Outside power and unequal relations fit Banda and Saint-Domingue. An imported object by itself would be insufficient to identify colonial rule.
The plural “processes” fits Ghana, Indonesia and Partition. Political handover can be dated separately from changes to local power and inequality.
Keeping, losing and providing access help explain the surviving Banda and Warsaw records. A gap in a collection cannot show that an event never happened.
Skill and work organization appear beside machines and energy, making this applicable to Tomioka as well as British factories. Different timings remain explicit.
Mounds and enclosures at Poverty Point and Hopewell fit the definition; neither shape nor size alone identifies their builders’ government.
Replaced a vague “limit after which” with the earliest possible date supported by evidence. The example dates the use of the specific timber and allows storage and reuse.
A reference curve and several possible calendar dates account for the Wendat graph. Calibration is distinguished from simply subtracting a radiocarbon age from a year.
Signs represent syllables, which explains why the Cherokee page has its own writing system. The definition does not imply that a bilingual page was readable by everyone.
The Onondaga account supplies situated meanings of belts and speakers. Recognizing shell beads does not permit an observer to assign a belt’s message independently.
Separates negotiation, signature and formal confirmation in Canandaigua. The text does not equate ratification with fulfillment of promises.
The Ojibwe name remains connected with food, cultural and spiritual significance. Naming the community accounts avoids claiming identical practices throughout the region.
Separation of grain from lighter chaff fits the Commission’s finishing sequence, distinct from other postharvest steps.
The comparison is between marine and contemporary terrestrial carbon; the need for local corrections is meaningful for the Bering Sea case.
The modern Hidatsa lodge and Inuinnait parkas show different uses of earlier evidence. Modern construction has its own date even when representing past practices.
Once-living material, calibration and environmental effects anchor the method in sampled remains. The caution about BP matters at Ozette.
Slow decay under persistently wet conditions explains why wood can survive at Ozette. The wording leaves room for selective survival.
Organized movements and activities across a year fit the Blackfoot landscape. Mobility is treated as work requiring knowledge rather than an absence of institutions.
An underground storage space connects Hidatsa agriculture to storage. An illustrative model cannot establish the contents of a particular excavated pit.
Return is situated in the account of Kwakwaka’wakw belongings. The definition encompasses ancestral remains without implying they are interchangeable with objects.
Witnessing and gifts are introduced through the named Kwakwaka’wakw account. Variation across Northwest Coast communities is explicit.
Stated conditions and a possible method fit the bison-processing experiment. The reader can distinguish experimental materials from an excavated event.
Shared material practices can be grouped across sites; a Hopewell or Bering Sea label alone cannot identify a state, language or unified nation.
The chemical-trace example fits the Chaco vessel inquiry. It requires a stated sample and alternative explanations before reconstructing a drink or practice.
The Pueblo context and variable form distinguish a cultural identification from a plan shape. A circular feature alone remains insufficient.
The lake-sediment example translates an indirect observation into everyday language. A changing signal does not count individual Cahokia residents.
The Cahokia entry identifies an analytical interpretation of ranked leadership. Neither an official title nor institutional unanimity follows from the term.
Quartz, clay and glassy material distinguish the Iznik ceramic body from porcelain. The definition does not purport to provide the selected dish’s recipe.
An Ottoman sultan’s emblem can involve calligraphy and decoration; the definition permits multiple skilled participants. It does not attribute the drawing to the sultan personally.
Coercion is explicit in the New Julfa and Cherokee cases. Later adaptation or success is kept separate from the conditions of removal.
Merchants, goods and an establishment make this more specific than a route. The term accommodates both urban and overland settings.
Learning institutions vary across Islamic societies. Bukhara’s surviving building requires further evidence for the curriculum or an individual student’s experience.
The protective finish is distinguished from the painted papier-mâché and pasteboard support in the Iranian dressing case. No chemical recipe is inferred.
Proclamation, foreign recognition and effective control can be investigated separately. This matters particularly for Indonesia’s 1945, 1949 and 1950 milestones.
Divided powers, subject to a particular agreement, fits the Indonesian settlement and Ghanaian debates. It does not imply equal power at each level.
The distinction between an announced standard and observed practice fits Qin measures. A rule does not establish immediate or universal adoption.
The term is explicitly attached to Ashoka’s messages on conduct and government. It avoids treating a selected edict as an exhaustive account of Buddhist belief.
The local Attic community and a specified fourth-century account prevent confusion with citizenship in any modern municipality. Enrollment is attributed to eligible men.
Relationships between layers and features explain why a deposit and its contents may have different dates. This applies to the Aksum and Caral examples.
Property or other resources can sustain an institution over time. At Nalanda, terms and maintenance require evidence beyond the surviving building.
Rotating service is distinguished from resettlement. Food supplied to Inca workers does not in itself measure how much choice they had.
The definition identifies the plural jeliw and includes multiple Mande performance roles. A particular performance retains its own audience and date.
Storage, preparation and delivery translate an abstract word into identifiable tasks. Egyptian and Moche cases can then be compared without assuming identical administration.
A woven plant-fiber bag is concrete; stone-filled examples belong specifically to Caral deposits. Bags cannot identify a labor obligation unaided.
Discarded material and layered occupation deposits are both intelligible at Skara Brae and Poverty Point. A midden requires its own formation history and dating.
Added non-clay material affects how pottery behaves. The Lapita case can consider material sources without inferring a named carrier or complete voyage.
Naming a category after a place differs from proving that the practice originated or spread from there. This distinction is directly relevant to Poverty Point.
Light pulses and elevation modeling explain how ground shapes become visible. Neither the model nor an observed mound supplies a construction date.
Quartz-rich glazed material is distinguishable from granite and ordinary clay. The Taharqo inquiry also needs object-specific evidence of manufacture.
The figure’s intended funerary work is clear. The words “intended” and “royal example” leave particular objects and beliefs open to specific investigation.
Added the reversal on the next row. The crosswise and lengthwise terms now allow the learner to follow both directions in the Chavín teaching diagram.
Connected rooms and open spaces can support multiple activities. At Teotihuacan the structure alone does not identify the size or legal status of a household.
Place, surrounding material and association distinguish archaeological context from style, ownership or museum location. This applies to the Colima figures.
Forms projecting from a background give a visible test applicable at Borobudur. The representation still requires evidence for use and interpretation.
Opposition can extend to destruction but takes different forms. The Byzantine entry attaches disputes to specific periods and policies.
Stone, bricks and different components of a wall are concrete. The Chaco construction does not identify its builders’ identities or governance by material alone.
Both a setting and a group of workers are possible. Catalogue attribution to an Ottoman or Mughal workshop supplies neither a roster nor ownership on its own.
